[LEXP.4.3] **A NaN's sign and payload are not observable.** IEEE 754 leaves
them to the hardware, so conforming engines produce NaNs that differ in both from
the same operands. The engine must not canonicalise them, and nothing a rule, a
recording or an integrator can read may depend on them: a NaN never reaches
working memory or a payload ([LEXP.4.2]), every NaN renders as `"nan"`
([LCST.4.5.6]), and `is NaN` tests the class alone ([LNUL.4.9]). A path that would expose a computed NaN's
bits must not be added.
